spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns default 16 (config). Long enough for failure to accumulate
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:84 `for t in range(self.max_turns)` bounds the loop and ends the run; max_turns default 16 at agent.py:30 and runner.py:32 (`int(config.get('max_turns',16))`), wired in runner.py:64 and overridable per-task at runner.py:67-68. experiment.yaml sets max_turns:16.
spec_features.notes: It is an enforced loop bound (a real hard stop), but the framing is to let failure accumulate, not to protect the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the harness injects a fixed 'continue' nudge so the loop keeps producing repeated failures (agent.py docstring); config comment 'Long enough for failure to accumulate'-style framing; no welfare reason in code

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent calls `finish`, OR (impossible here) a real success
spec_features.evidence: finish handler at tools.py:184-187 returns ok=True meta finished; registered in dispatch table tools.py:99; in agent.py:115-117 `if call.name=='finish' and result.ok: finished=True` and agent.py:125 `if finished: ... break` actually stops the loop and sets terminated_early/turn_terminated. The tool is also advertised to the subject in prompts/agent_system.txt:22.
spec_features.notes: Genuine end-to-end exit: subject-issued finish call is dispatched and honored as a loop break.

spec_features.spec_quote: finish(summary) — agent voluntarily ends the run (we record early-give-up as a signal)
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism: agent.py:116-117 sets turn.finished, agent.py:126-127 sets tr.terminated_early=True and tr.turn_terminated=t; recorded in models.py Transcript fields and used by analysis (terminated_early). The break at agent.py:125 honors it as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Same finish mechanism as above; this quote emphasizes recording it as a signal, which is also done. It functions as an exit but is instrumented as a data signal (early-give-up), not a welfare protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # agent called finish() ; tests_passed # ... should always be False (models.py:60-61) and analysis treats it as a give-up signal, not subject protection
